description: Anonymised samples of real Pakistani bank SMS formats. `expectedType` is the direction parseBankMessage() should hint at, or null when the message carries no usable signal. Account numbers, names and amounts are invented.

cases.name: HBL debit card purchase at a merchant
cases.message: HBL: Your Debit Card ending 1234 has been debited with PKR 1,500.00 at KFC on 15-01-24. Available Balance: PKR 50,000.00
cases.note: Classic debit alert; 'debited' plus an available balance.

cases.name: POS purchase on a card
cases.message: POS purchase of PKR 850.00 made at METRO on card ending 4321.

cases.name: ATM cash withdrawal
cases.message: Your account has been debited with PKR 20,000 via ATM withdrawal on 2024-01-15.

cases.name: Person-to-person transfer sent
cases.message: UBL: You have sent PKR 5,000 to ALI RAZA (03001234567) on 15/01/2024. TID: 987654
cases.note: The phrasing the user called out — 'you have sent' must read as an expense.

cases.name: Transfer out using 'transferred to'
cases.message: PKR 12,000 transferred to AHMED KHAN on 15-01-2024. Ref: 55221
cases.note: 'transferred to' is direction-specific; a bare 'transferred' would be ambiguous.

cases.name: Transfer to a person, sending bank named in the message
cases.message: Alfalah Bank: Rs.1,200.00 transferred to HASSAN from your account on 14-10-2026. Available balance: PKR 8,400.00
cases.note: The reported failure: the sending bank is the loudest name in the message, but the counterparty is HASSAN. 'Alfalah Bank' must never become the transaction's merchant.

cases.name: Salary credited
cases.message: PKR 25,000.00 credited to your account 01234567890 on 15-Jan-2024. Salary for Jan 2024.

cases.name: Wallet receive
cases.message: Easypaisa: You have received Rs. 2,000 from BILAL (03451234567). New balance Rs. 3,500.
cases.note: 'you have received' — the mirror of the sent case.

cases.name: Transfer in using 'transferred from'
cases.message: PKR 8,500 transferred from SANA MALIK to your account on 15-01-2024.
cases.note: 'transferred from' must not be caught by the 'transferred to' debit rule.

cases.name: Merchant refund
cases.message: Refund of PKR 1,200 has been credited to your card ending 5678 at DARAZ on 15-01-2024.
cases.note: A refund is money coming back in, not an expense.

cases.name: Signed negative amount, no verb
cases.message: Transaction of Rs. -1,500 on your account 0123 on 15-01-2024.
cases.note: The minus sign is the only signal; the amount regex must not skip it.

cases.name: 'caused' must not be read as 'used'
cases.message: Refund of PKR 1,200 credited to your account. Delay caused by bank.
cases.note: Regression: substring matching on 'used' matched inside 'caused', and debit was checked first, so this used to resolve to expense.

cases.name: 'unused' must not be read as 'used'
cases.message: Your card ending 1234 is unused since 01-01-2024. No transactions this month.

cases.name: Conflicting signals in one message
cases.message: You have received PKR 500 refund. Your account was debited PKR 1,500.
cases.note: Debit and credit both present, so the hint is withheld and the AI decides unaided.

cases.name: Balance notification with no direction
cases.message: Your account 01234567890 balance is PKR 12,345.00 as of 15-01-2024.
cases.note: A balance statement is not a transaction; no direction may be inferred.
